$comment: Canonical module types for the shift / sub-shift reading views.
A shift page is an ordered list of {type, data} modules; this file is the
contract between the pipeline (which emits them) and the front end (which
renders them). Adding a type means: add it here, emit it from the pipeline's
MODULE_TEMPLATE, and register a component in
apps/frontend/src/shift/modules.jsx. Unknown types fail publication and the
front end also surfaces a defensive unavailable-section fallback.
One type breaks that pattern: `innovations` is not generated at all. The
backend hydrates it into each shift row when it builds a route fragment, so
an innovation pushed by the upstream database appears within the response
cache TTL instead of waiting for the next weekly publication. The order
below is still what decides where it lands — apps/backend/src/innovations.rs
mirrors these two lists as consts and a test fails if they drift.
$order_comment: Canonical reading order, from the Miro content mockup (SERIOUS SHIFT 2026 →
Content Mockup- July'26). The export sorts every module list by this, so
changing the order here re-composes each page on the next --export-only with
no regeneration. Types absent from a page are simply skipped.
Note the sub-shift carousel sits at the BOTTOM of a shift page.

lede.summary: Opening line of a sub-shift page.

from_to.summary: The shift's spine as two cards whose gradient fills cross-fade.

from_to_solid.summary: From/To pair with solid green/pink fills (sub-shift variant).

stat_band.summary: Full-bleed band: oversized numeral, prose, source.

peel_tabs.summary: Two stacked cards the reader toggles: what's changing / why now.

sub_shift_list.summary: Cards linking to this shift's sub-shifts. Resolved from context, not data.

human_needs.summary: Two expanding cards: the need unlocked and the need threatened.

tension_band.summary: Dark full-bleed band carrying the consumer tension, in the consumer's own voice.

pull_quote.summary: The editorial line that lands the shift, set immediately after From/To. Distinct from tension_band: this is the analyst's verdict, not the consumer's voice.

innovations.summary: "Innovations in the wild" — real branded examples of the shift, from the innovations table. Not generated: the backend hydrates this module's items from innovation_shift_links when it builds a route fragment, so a newly-ingested example appears without a publication run. `image` is always a same-origin /api/innovations/{id}/cover-image path, because the CSP is img-src 'self'.

timeline.summary: Now / next / beyond, as a vertical timeline.

industries.summary: Sector chips plus a detail card that swaps on selection.

territories.summary: Opportunity-territory cards plus a work-with-us card.

signals.summary: Numbered evidence that the shift is real (sub-shift).

voices.summary: Who backs this shift and who disputes it, with their own words. Built at export from the thinker-attribution phase — no extra model spend.

evidence.summary: The sourced claims behind a sub-shift: what was said, by whom, where, and when. Distinct from `signals`, which is written prose.

related_shifts.summary: Typed links to other shifts (reinforces, accelerated_by, …) from the interrelatedness phase.

rich_text.summary: Escape hatch for editor-authored prose. Never generated.

$sectors_comment: The 16 TrendWatching sectors. The industries module asks for one entry per sector, in this order; kt_editorial.txt must match this list.
